title: Short-cycle slab exposure and inventory hire sensitivity - Mar 2026
content:
Executive summary:
This is a working sandbox exploring short-cycle slab exposure (weekly/monthly small slabs) and the implied headcount inventory needed to sustain burst capacity without breaking price floors. Goal: quantify marginal unit economics of micro-slabs vs. reserved capacity and provide hire/contracting guidance for a 12-week sprint window.

Key context / why now:
- Marketing pilot for new PLG tier (micro-slab) launching Q2 2026; expected sporadic, high-variance demand from small customers.
- We need a negative-test plan if take-rate is higher than modeled (fast burn).
- This doc pairs pricing sensitivity (per-1k token price bands) with short-cycle staffing (contractor vs FTE mix) and GPU inventory shadowing.

Core assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline token yield per 1k tokens revenue: $0.012 (hosted API micro-slab price baseline).
- Cost per 1k tokens (average mixed model: quantized Llama-2-13B-ish serving): $0.006 at steady-state; rises to $0.011 under microburst tail because of spot/reserve spillover.
- Micro-slab product expected take-rate scenarios: low 5% conversion, mid 15%, high 30% of free-trial cohort.
- Typical slab size definition: 100k tokens/month (small customers).
- Latency SLO requires burst capacity within 500ms p95; supporting burst requires warmable GPU pools (inventory).
- Average GPU-hour cost (cloud blended, incl infra): $2.8/hr. Median throughput: 250k tokens/hr per GPU (in quantized mode).

Snapshot tables (working numbers — keep as cells for copy/paste):

Pricing sensitivity by slab take-rate (monthly):
Scenario | est customers | avg tokens/customer | total monthly tokens | rev per 1k | revenue | blended cost per 1k | cost | gross margin
Baseline-low | 1,200 | 100,000 | 120,000,000 | $0.012 | $1,440 | $0.006 | $720 | $720 (50%)
Baseline-mid | 3,600 | 100,000 | 360,000,000 | $0.012 | $4,320 | $0.007 | $2,520 | $1,800 (41.7%)
Baseline-high | 7,200 | 100,000 | 720,000,000 | $0.012 | $8,640 | $0.009 | $6,480 | $2,160 (25%)

Note: blended cost per 1k rises with higher bursts because we spill into on-demand or reserved-burst bands; see sensitivity below.

Headcount and inventory mapping (12-week sprint lens):
Role | baseline FTEs (current) | incremental contractors needed (12w surge) | delta cost (12w)
Infra ops (warm pools) | 4 | 2 contractors | $120k
SRE (runbooks & incident) | 3 | 1 contractor | $30k
Customer success | 6 | 3 contractors (onboarding) | $45k
Billing & finance | 2 | 0.5 contractor | $12k
Total incremental cost (12w) | - | - | $207k

GPU inventory shadow (equivalent hours required for burst headroom):
- Baseline-mid month tokens -> 360M tokens -> ~1,440 GPU-hrs/month (360M / 250k) ~48 GPU-hrs/day.
- High scenario -> 720M tokens -> ~2,880 GPU-hrs/month -> need doubling of warmable pool.
- Warmable pool cost delta (steady -> burst) dominated by reserved vs on-demand mix. Example delta: additional 48 GPU-hrs/day at $2.8/hr => $4k/day -> $120k/month.

Pricing sensitivity matrix (per-1k token price variation):
Price band | margin @ baseline-mid (cost @ $0.007) | margin @ mid but cost increases (spills to $0.009)
$0.010 | negative (-14%) | -36%
$0.012 | +42% | +22%
$0.014 | +66% | +46%

Break-even slab price under high-burst costs:
- If blended cost climbs to $0.011/1k (high spill), break-even revenue per 1k = $0.011 (0% margin). To restore 30% gross margin, price must be >= $0.0157/1k.

Inventory hire sensitivity (what to hire vs contract):
- Rule-of-thumb recommended mix for 12-week product launch: 60% contractors for infra/sre/onboarding (fast ramp & fall-back), 40% FTEs prioritized to CS & billing for retention.
- Rationale: contractors allow quick shrink after pilot, minimizing long-term OTE. If take-rate > 20% sustained beyond two quarters, convert 50% of contractor capacity to FTEs.

Stress tests run (notes):
- ST1: Sudden 3x volume week in week 2 of launch. Observed: cost per 1k rose from $0.007 -> $0.013 due to on-demand spill and preemption fallback. Margin negative at baseline price.
- ST2: 40% of trial customers double slab consumption. Observed: onboarding ops become bottleneck; CS ticket time x2; potential churn if not staffed.
- ST3: Regional imbalance where EU demand concentrated -> regional capacity premiums +20% cost.

Recommendations (immediate):
1) Pricing: add a contingency surcharge band for micro-slabs if monthly tokens move above 150k/customer or if warmable pool utilization >65% (suggest +12–20% price band).
2) Inventory hedges: pre-warm a small reserved slot pool sized for mid scenario (approx +50 GPUs for initial 12 weeks) and enable auto-fallback pricing to customers (notify them of degraded performance SLA if fallback occurs).
3) Hiring posture: engage 8–10 short-term contractors (infra/SRE/CS) with defined conversion windows; start recruiting two senior infra FTEs (long-lead).
4) Billing guardrail: implement dynamic chargeback flags for customers consuming >250k tokens/month to route to sales and apply manual quota + pricing review.
5) Runbook: add a capacity truss checklist to SRE runbooks (warm pools, KV cache priming, soft-fallback model).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Validate per-token cost model with applied-ml team for the selected quantized runtime (ticket: JIRA-FIN-2107).
- Confirm ability to programmatically present surcharge in UI for micro-slabs (product/console ticket: CON-UX-512).
- Build quick dashboard (console) to show slab utilization and warm-pool fill in real-time for finance gating.
- Legal check on billing contract language for dynamic surcharges (legal@redwood).

Appendix: quick sensitivity snapshots (copyable)
- Unit economics formula used: margin = (price_per_1k - cost_per_1k) * (total_tokens/1000) - incremental_staff_costs - additional_gpu_inventory_costs.
- Example calculation (baseline-mid):
  price=0.012, cost=0.007, tokens=360,000,000 -> gross margin tokens = (0.005)*(360,000) = $1,800 -> subtract incremental 12w pro-rated = ($207k / 3 months) ~= $69k -> Adjusted margin ~= $1,731 (negative once infra months counted differently; need to spread correctly).

Notes to reviewers: rough draft numbers. Please annotate cells with corrections. Prefer a quick sync with applied-ml and product this week (Mar 16–18).
